chunks: Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Abī al-Ward, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a woman who is in salat al-ẓuhr and has prayed two rakʿahs, then she sees blood. He said: “She rises from her place of prayer and does not make up the two rakʿahs.”

He said: “But if she sees blood while she is in salat al-maghrib and she has prayed two rakʿahs, then she should rise from her place of prayer; and when she becomes pure, she should make up the one rakʿah that she missed from al-maghrib.”

key_terms.الرَّكْعَةَ: the single unit of prayer remaining
key_terms.تَقْضِ: she makes up or performs as qaḍāʾ
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer already completed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman sees menstrual blood during ẓuhr or maghrib prayer after praying two rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who begins menstruation during salat. If this occurs after two rakʿahs of ẓuhr, she leaves the prayer and does not make up those two rakʿahs, but if it occurs after two rakʿahs of maghrib, she later makes up the remaining one rakʿah after attaining taharah.
